q: In Galatians, what is the first fruit of the Spirit Paul lists?
quote: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace

q: In Galatians, which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
quote: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness

q: In Galatians, what is the last fruit of the Spirit Paul lists?
quote: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

q: In Galatians, against the fruit of the Spirit there is no what?
quote: Against such things there is no law.

q: In Galatians, the fruit of the Spirit comes from whom?
quote: But the fruit of the Spirit is love

q: In Galatians, if you walk by the Spirit, what will you not gratify?
quote: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.

q: In Galatians, since we live by the Spirit, we should walk in step with whom?
quote: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.

q: In Galatians, Paul warns walkers in the Spirit not to become what?
quote: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.

q: In Galatians, Paul tells believers to carry one another's what?
why: This fulfills the law of Christ.
quote: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

q: In Galatians, Paul says all believers are one in whom?
quote: for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

q: In Galatians, Paul says do not grow weary in doing what?
quote: Let us not grow weary in well-doing

q: In Galatians, Paul says he no longer lives, but who lives in him?
quote: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.

q: In Galatians, for what has Christ set us free?
quote: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free.

q: In Galatians, how should believers use their freedom?
quote: Rather, serve one another in love.

q: In Galatians, the entire law is fulfilled in which single command?
quote: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

q: In Galatians, whatever a man sows, he will do what?
quote: Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.

q: In Galatians, Paul says the righteous will live by what?
why: No one is justified by the law.
quote: because, “The righteous will live by faith.”

q: In Galatians, when the time had fully come, whom did God send?
why: Born of a woman, under the law.
quote: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son

q: In Galatians, Paul will boast only in what?
why: Through it the world is crucified to him.
quote: But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ

q: To which churches did Paul write the letter of Galatians?
why: Galatia was a region, not one city.
quote: To the churches of Galatia

q: In Galatians, how many days did Paul stay with Cephas in Jerusalem?
why: It was three years after his call.
quote: and I stayed with him fifteen days.

q: In Galatians, in which city did Paul oppose Cephas to his face?
quote: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face

q: In Galatians, what did Paul say about the letters he wrote with his own hand?
quote: See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!

q: In Galatians, where did Paul go after his call, before returning to Damascus?
why: He did not go to Jerusalem first.
quote: but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.

q: In Galatians, James, Cephas, and John were esteemed as what?
why: They gave Paul the right hand of fellowship.
quote: James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship
